solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cereal with taste of umami for a sauce

indicators.note: 'X for Y' tells the solver to put one letter in place of another inside the word

parts.note: sago is a starchy cereal-like food from palm pith

indicators.note: a taste is only a small sample, so just the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter, its 'taste', of umami
the letter A, taken as written, is the one swapped out

explanation.surface: A cook seasons a cereal dish with umami flavour to turn it into a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with taste of umami for a' means: in SAGO, put the U of umami where the A was.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugo is the Italian word for a sauce, especially a tomato pasta sauce, listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Clamour once United press on the counter

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: going counter means running the opposite way, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: to sit on something is to press it down

explanation.surface: A newspaper cuttings counter at United's ground is besieged by a noisy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the definition as obsolete: utis is an old word, found in Shakespeare, for a din or uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Utis is an archaic noun for noisy merriment or uproar, matching an old-fashioned word for din.

clue.text: Happy place? Fancy not once returning

parts.note: 'Fancy!' and 'Gosh!' are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: NE is an archaic word for not

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cheerful spot exists and is told, fancifully, not once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' flags an archaic word: NE meant not in older English.
explanation.definitionFit: Goshen was the fertile Biblical land given to the Israelites in Egypt, so the name stands for any place of plenty and contentment.

clue.text: Anything Scottish? Brooch with drop of thistle

parts.note: an ouch is an old word for a brooch or clasp set with jewels

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only one letter, the first, is taken from this word

parts.note: the first letter of thistle

explanation.surface: Is anything more Scottish than a brooch decorated with a thistle?
explanation.walkthrough: The thistle is Scotland's emblem, so the surface paints a Scottish brooch while the answer is simply a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oucht is a Scots form of aught, meaning anything at all, so it is the Scottish word for anything.

clue.text: With shoes off, very laid back with cat snuggling close to fire

indicators.note: something snuggling is nestled inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: to cat is slang for to vomit, and barf means the same

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so just the last letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of fire

indicators.note: laid back here is taken literally as set down backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: too means very, as in too kind

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes shoeless, feeling very laid back with the cat curled up close to the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is not a pet: to cat is British slang for being sick, so the cosy fireside scene hides a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Barefoot describes someone wearing nothing on their feet, which is the state of having taken shoes off.

clue.text: Safari, perhaps right to be tapping water supply?

indicators.note: tapping a supply means drawing from it by getting inside, so one letter goes into the other word

parts.note: a bowser is a tanker carrying water or fuel
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: On a safari, is it right to tap a water supply in the bush?
explanation.walkthrough: Safari is not a trip to see animals but Apple's web browser; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Safari is a named example of software for viewing web pages, the general class being a browser.

clue.text: Informal meeting of scientists, current one's starting

definitions.note: a rencounter is any casual meeting; the scientists are surface colour

indicators.note: starting can mean jumping or moving suddenly, so the letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: At an informal gathering of scientists, a current talk is just getting under way.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the two words current one; nothing in the clue's science setting supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives rencounter as a chance or casual meeting, an older form of the French rencontre.

clue.text: Work with utility company around outskirts of Reading

indicators.note: around means going round the outside, so one word wraps another

parts.note: E.ON is a large energy supplier in the UK

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters of Reading

explanation.surface: Someone works for a utility company on the edge of Reading, a large English town.
explanation.walkthrough: E.ON is an energy company serving UK homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergon is a Greek-derived word for work or business, the root that also gives the physics unit erg.

clue.text: Founder of colony's old English tomb

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English
a cist is a prehistoric stone coffin or burial chamber

explanation.surface: The ancient English tomb of a colony's founder is unearthed.
explanation.definitionFit: An oecist was the leader who established a new settlement in ancient Greece, so the term names a colonial founder.

clue.text: Man in love with Pearl, perhaps bewitched

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: a pearl is one kind of bead
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man falls in love with a woman called Pearl and seems bewitched.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like O; 'Pearl, perhaps' is a definition by example, a pearl being one kind of bead.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of Caribbean sorcery, and to obeah someone is to cast a spell on them, so obeahed means bewitched.

clue.text: Dodge perhaps after time and mouths outdated language

indicators.note: after puts the car second, following the abbreviation for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Dodge is an American make of car
ora is the Latin plural of os, a mouth

explanation.surface: A dodge involving time and talk is dismissed as old-fashioned speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodge perhaps' gives US CAR, an American car; it comes after T, with ORA joined on by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscarora is an Iroquoian Native American language with very few remaining speakers, so it is now largely out of use.

clue.text: Toured around Great Lake blundering

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A tourist travelling around one of the Great Lakes keeps making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in ERIE too, not just toured.
explanation.definitionFit: Étourderie is a French loan word for heedless thoughtlessness or a careless slip, matching blundering as a noun.

clue.text: Spirit drink recalled by company

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: to sip is to drink
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A spirit drink is recalled by the company that produced it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisco is a grape brandy made in Peru and Chile, a type of distilled alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Characters in some strange, lost Syriac alphabet

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, inside the following words spell out the answer

parts.note: found running across these words

explanation.surface: Some strange, lost characters turn out to come from a Syriac alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangelo is the oldest style of script used for writing Syriac, an Aramaic language of the early Christian Middle East.

clue.text: Sorbets lacking special flavours?

indicators.note: lacking means without, so some letters are taken away

parts.note: spices give food flavour
SP is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Are these sorbets without any special flavours?
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a frozen dessert of sweetened fruit juice, which the British also call a water ice.

clue.text: One of the Three Musketeers maybe downs arms in action

definitions.text: One of the Three Musketeers maybe

indicators.note: things in action are moving about, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: One of Dumas's Three Musketeers lays down his weapons in the middle of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Musketeers in Dumas's novel are expert fencers, so each is an example of a skilled fighter with a blade.

clue.text: Largely reckoning first clue's drossy?

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a score is a reckoning or tally
the puzzle's first clue is 1 across, written 1 AC with the digit as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A solver wonders whether the first clue, by most reckonings, is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first clue' is taken literally as the label 1 AC, the opening clue of this very puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoria is the slag or clinker left from smelting, so the adjective scoriac means like dross; Poe uses it in Ulalume.

clue.text: Spread teeth with snow — stimulant …

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spreads toothpaste-white snow over teeth and calls it a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue but adds nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetstone sharpens blades, so figuratively it is anything that sharpens the wits or spurs one on.

clue.text: … has spread front to back

indicators.note: moving the front to the back shifts the opening letter to the end of the word

parts.note: seed that is sown has been spread over a field

explanation.surface: Continuing from the clue before, it is about what is spread from front to back.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, so owns works as a synonym for has in the third person.

clue.text: Spinning thread — some section to be cut for red carpet?

indicators.note: spinning turns something round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a clew is a ball of thread; it is reversed

indicators.note: cut means removed, so a letter is taken out of the neighbouring word

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: Someone spinning thread trims a section of a long red carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that red carpet stands for the treatment it signals rather than a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet is the idiom for giving an important guest a lavish reception, a grand greeting.

clue.text: Butler's busy brushing off black coat

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling about, so the letters are moved into a new order
brushing something off removes it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, dropping the apostrophe
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A busy butler brushes the dust off a black coat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose, heavy overcoat, often belted, named after the Irish province.

clue.text: Butcher's can seek stews

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: stewing something mixes it up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A butcher is able to look for stewing meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look, so having a butcher's means taking a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is informal for a quick look, the same thing a British speaker means by a butcher's.

clue.text: Obstacle's concerning delay

parts.note: re means concerning or about
mora is a legal term for delay, especially in meeting an obligation

explanation.surface: A report on what is causing a hold-up in a project.
explanation.definitionFit: Remora is an old word for a hindrance, from the sucker fish once believed to slow down ships.

clue.text: Cook simmer — repetition of parts?

indicators.note: to cook is also to falsify or doctor, so the letters are tampered with

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cook, then simmer, repeating parts of the method.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a merism is the repeating of similar parts within one organism, such as body segments.

clue.text: Vegetable silage husked and turned over

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the letters are read backwards
husking strips the outer layer, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: silage is animal fodder

explanation.surface: A farmer husks a vegetable and turns it over among the silage.
explanation.definitionFit: The eddo is the edible starchy tuber of the taro plant, eaten as a root crop.

clue.text: Over four times a day, starts to use any trusted herbicide

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: QID, Latin quater in die, is a prescription note for four doses daily

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so just the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A gardener applies a trusted weedkiller more than four times a day.
explanation.walkthrough: QID is the doctors' abbreviation on prescriptions for four times daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Diquat is a chemical weedkiller used to clear vegetation and dry crops before harvest.

clue.text: One building bridges over Tasmanian mountain range pressing forward!

parts.note: 'pon is a shortened form of upon, which means over

indicators.note: pressing into something means pushing inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Chambers lists tier as a Tasmanian term for a mountain range
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A bridge builder working over a Tasmanian mountain range pushes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pon is a poetic clipping of upon. Tier as a mountain range is a Tasmanian usage that Chambers records.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontonier is a military engineer who builds pontoon bridges, so he constructs crossings for a living.

clue.text: Shabby person completely stalling response

indicators.note: stalling something holds it in a stall, so one word is held inside another

parts.note: out means completely, as in tired out
in Chinese medicine bi is a pattern of bodily response, a term Chambers records

explanation.surface: A scruffy person keeps delaying an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives oubit as a hairy caterpillar and, by extension, a scruffy or unkempt individual.

clue.text: Almost nothing starts to leaf across ravine …

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: null means nothing or void

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the first letter of each word counts

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Almost nothing begins to drift, leaf by leaf, across a gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nulla, or nullah, is an Indian word for a watercourse or steep gully, a dry ravine.

clue.text: Local crowd that is heralding touchdown at Eton

parts.note: sc, from Latin scilicet, means namely or that is
a rouge is a scoring move in the Eton field game, a little like a try

explanation.surface: At Eton, a crowd of local boys cheers a touchdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boarding school with its own football games. 'Local' means the word is dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrouge is a dialect verb meaning to squeeze or press together, the same sense as to crowd someone.

clue.text: … fertile plain's area with food plants

parts.note: veg is short for vegetables
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a fertile plain is a region with crops growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area with food plants' puts A after VEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is a Spanish word for a low, well-watered stretch of farmland, used in English for such valleys.

clue.text: Local Labour MP's opening news …

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of MP
in Australian slang the good oil is reliable information or news

explanation.surface: A local Labour Party MP makes an opening announcement to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is not the British political party but plain toil, and 'Local' marks the answer as dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Moil is a dialect word for drudgery or hard toil, as in toil and moil.

clue.text: … having fallen heavily, MP's denied being drunk

indicators.note: something denied is withheld, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: to slump is to fall heavily
taken as written

explanation.surface: After collapsing in a heap, an MP denies being drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slued, also spelt slewed, is slang for intoxicated, as if lurching sideways like a swung boat.

clue.text: Decoy to linger in what club?

parts.note: a shill is an accomplice posing as a customer to lure others

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: eh is a way of saying what? when you have not heard
to lag is to linger or fall behind

explanation.surface: Someone asks which club a decoy is hanging around in.
explanation.definitionFit: A shillelagh is an Irish cudgel of blackthorn or oak, a stout wooden stick used as a weapon.

clue.text: Worm's broken back into point on network

indicators.note: back means backwards, so this word is reversed
into places one piece inside another

parts.note: a node is a junction point in a network
a horse that is broken is tame; TAME is reversed

explanation.surface: A worm has broken back into a point on a computer network.
explanation.walkthrough: Broken means tamed, as with a horse; reversed TAME goes inside NODE after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nematodes are roundworms, a large group of unsegmented worms, many of them parasites.

clue.text: Thatcher leaves thanks protected by American plan

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed within it

parts.note: AP is a hotel rate abbreviation, American plan, covering room and all meals
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher leaves office, sheltered by an American plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher is not the British prime minister but someone who thatches roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: Atap is the Malay name for nipa palm leaves used as roofing material, the foliage a roof-maker works with.
